result.markdown: --- title: "[NegativeBinomial]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Negative Binomial family with log link (NB2 parameterization). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/negative_binomial.py#L13-L155){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python NegativeBinomial(theta=1.0) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The Negative Binomial family models count data that is overdispersed relative to the Poisson distribution, i.e. where the observed variance exceeds the mean. This commonly arises when counts are driven by unobserved heterogeneity across observations (e.g. some individuals or locations are systematically more prone to events than others). Whittaker uses the NB2 parameterization, where the variance function is `V(mu) = mu + mu^2/theta` and `theta` controls the degree of overdispersion: as `theta -> infinity` the distribution converges to `Poisson`, while smaller `theta` implies heavier overdispersion. The canonical log link is used, giving the same multiplicative interpretation of coefficients as `Poisson`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [theta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Overdispersion (size) parameter, must be positive. Smaller values of `theta` imply greater overdispersion; larger values make the distribution approach `Poisson`. The value supplied at construction is used as the starting point and is refined during fitting via an outer iteration around P-IRLS unless explicitly held fixed by the caller. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} The canonical link is the natural logarithm: $$ g(\mu) = \log(\mu) $$ The variance function is $$ V(\mu) = \mu + \frac{\mu^2}{\theta}, $$ so the variance always exceeds the mean by the extra term $\mu^2/\theta$. The deviance is $$ D(y, \hat\mu) = 2 \sum_i \left[ y_i \log\!\left(\frac{y_i}{\hat\mu_i}\right) - (y_i + \theta) \log\!\left(\frac{y_i + \theta}{\hat\mu_i + \theta}\right) \right] . $$ ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a GAM to overdispersed count data: ::: {#5f509bf7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import whittaker as wk rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 200 x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n) mu = np.exp(0.5 * np.sin(x)) theta = 3.0 y = rng.negative_binomial(theta, theta / (theta + mu)) data = {"x": x, "y": y} model = wk.GAM("y ~ s(x)", family=wk.NegativeBinomial(theta=theta)) model.fit(data, method="REML") print(model.summary()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` GAM fit summary ============================================================ Formula: y ~ s(x) Family: NegativeBinomial(theta=4.721, link='log') Observations: 200 Coefficients: 10 Parametric coefficients: Term Estimate Std.Err z value p-value ------------------------ ---------- ---------- ---------- ---------- (Intercept) -0.0054 0.0792 -0.069 0.9451 Approximate significance of smooth terms: Term EDF Ref.df Chi.sq p-value ------------------------ ------ ------ ---------- ---------- s(x) 3.54 4 15.493 0.003781 Total EDF: 4.54 Deviance: 210.5567 Null dev: 229.3245 Dev. expl: 8.2% GCV score: 1.102291 Scale est: 1.000000 AIC: 543.06 BIC: 558.05 ``` ::: :::
